title: Which tea is more expensive?
description: Himachal tea costs two hundred rupees for two hundred grams and Meghalaya tea costs eight hundred rupees for one kilogram. The video puts both weights in one unit, tests the two ratios, and finds the price of one kilogram of each. Keeko doubts this and compares only the prices.
teaching_notes: One idea: two prices can be compared only for the same weight, so both weights go into one unit first. Watch for students who compare two hundred with eight hundred and ignore that the weights are different.

source: Himachal tea costs ₹200 for 200 g. Meghalaya tea costs ₹800
video_script.why: The child sees that prices for different weights cannot be compared directly, and that a ratio test and a one kilogram price both settle which tea is dearer.
video_script.substitution: Write both weights in grams, form the two ratios, test them by cross multiplying, and find the price of one kilogram of each tea.
video_script.anchor: two packets of tea, one from Himachal and one from Meghalaya, from the book
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko compares eight hundred rupees with two hundred rupees without noticing that the two prices are for different weights.

final_answer.value: Himachal tea is more expensive: ₹1000 a kg against ₹800 a kg
final_answer.spoken: Himachal tea is more expensive, at one thousand rupees a kilogram against eight hundred rupees a kilogram

never_show: 800 > 200 so Meghalaya tea is more expensive, marked as right
maths_rules: 1 kg = 1000 g; weight : price is 200 : 200 for Himachal and 1000 : 800 for Meghalaya
cross multiplying: 1 × 4 = 4 and 5 × 1 = 5, not equal, so not proportional
Himachal: 1000 g ÷ 200 g = 5; 5 × 200 = 1000 rupees for 1 kg
1000 rupees is more than 800 rupees for 1 kg
video_script.design: One idea: compare prices for the same weight. The two packets stay on the stage and the working sits on the board.

narration: <bookmark mark='unit'/>Step one, change one kilogram to one thousand grams.
<bookmark mark='ratios'/>The ratios of weight to price are two hundred to two hundred, and one thousand to eight hundred.
<bookmark mark='simp'/>Step two, write each ratio in its simplest form. Himachal is one to one, and Meghalaya is five to four.

marks.cross: 1 × 4 = 4 and 5 × 1 = 5 are written with a not-equal sign between them

narration: <bookmark mark='cross'/>Step three, cross multiply. One times four is four, and five times one is five.
The two ratios are not equal, so the prices are not in proportion.

marks.five: 1000 ÷ 200 = 5 is written beside the small packet
marks.price: 5 × 200 = 1000 is written and 800 is written beside the bigger packet

narration: <bookmark mark='five'/>Step four, find the Himachal price for one kilogram. One kilogram is five times as much as two hundred grams.
<bookmark mark='price'/>The price is also five times as much, which is one thousand rupees. Meghalaya tea costs eight hundred rupees for the same weight.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Himachal tea is more expensive: 1000 rupees for 1 kg against 800 rupees for 1 kg
